question: What is the difference between recursive and iterative DNS resolution, and which one does this resolver do?
answer_hinglish:
Dono ek hi kaam ke do roles hain. Recursive query mein client (nslookup, OS stub) bolta hai: "mujhe poora answer chahiye, tum khud dhoondo" -- isliye woh RD=1 (Recursion Desired) bhejta hai. Iterative query mein resolver ek authoritative server se poochta hai aur server sirf apni jaankari deta hai: answer, ya "main nahi jaanta, in servers se poocho" (referral). Server kisi aur se khud nahi poochta.

Yeh project dono side dikhata hai. Client ki taraf se yeh ek recursive resolver hai: src/server.ts RD=1 wali query leta hai aur RA=1 ke saath poora answer deta hai. Upstream ki taraf yeh iterative hai: Resolver.resolve root se shuru karta hai, root ek referral deta hai (test TLD ke servers), TLD ek aur referral deta hai (alpha.test ke servers), aur aakhri server answer deta hai. Har upstream query buildQuery(randomId(), name, type, false) se banti hai, yaani RD=0.

RD=0 kyun? Kyunki hum authoritative servers se baat kar rahe hain; unse recursion maangna galat hai (zyada tar mana kar denge ya REFUSED denge), aur agar hum kisi doosre recursive resolver ko RD=1 bhejte toh woh "forwarder" ban jaata, khud resolve karna nahi. Test "follows root -> test -> alpha.test referrals using glue, with RD=0 on every query" fake network ke har server ke log mein rd false check karta hai, aur mutation R10 (queries RD=1 ke saath) isi test ne pakda.
why_needed: Interview mein yeh pehla sawaal hota hai: tum forwarder ho ya asli resolver? Iterative walk samjhe bina referral, glue, zone cut kuch samajh nahi aata.
real_world_analogy: Recursive: aap receptionist ko bolte ho 'is aadmi ka number la do', woh khud dhoondhti hai. Iterative: receptionist bolti hai 'mujhe nahi pata, HR floor par poocho', HR bolta hai 'team lead se poocho' -- aap khud ek ek floor jaate ho.
how_it_works: Client -> stub server (RD=1) -> Resolver.resolve -> root (RD=0) -> referral -> TLD (RD=0) -> referral -> zone server (RD=0) -> answer -> cache -> client ko RA=1 ke saath answer.
in_this_project: src/resolver.ts ki file comment: 'Iterative ("recursive" from the client's point of view) resolution, starting at the root servers.' exchange() mein buildQuery(..., false). Test 'follows root -> test -> alpha.test referrals using glue, with RD=0 on every query' 3 queries aur rd=false assert karta hai. README mutation R10.
advantages: Kisi upstream resolver par bharosa nahi, khud root se verify
Har step trace mein dikhta hai, debugging aasaan
Authoritative servers ke saath sahi protocol behaviour
disadvantages: Cold cache par zyada queries (root, TLD, zone) aur zyada latency
Forwarder se zyada code: referral, glue, limits sab khud
common_mistakes: RD bit ko 'recursive ho ya nahi' ki jagah 'server recursion karega' samajhna
Upstream ko bhi RD=1 bhej dena
Socha ki authoritative server khud aage poochta hai
follow_up_questions: Forwarding resolver (kisi upstream public resolver ko RD=1) aur yeh design mein kya farak hai?
RA bit kaun set karta hai aur kyun?
Agar koi authoritative server RD=1 query ka jawab de de toh kya hota hai?

question: What are root hints, why does the resolver need them, and why is a hard-coded list acceptable?
answer_hinglish:
Root hints woh starting point hain jahan se har cold lookup shuru hota hai: 13 root server names (a.root-servers.net se m.root-servers.net) aur unke addresses. Resolver ko kisi bhi naam ke liye pehle kisi se poochna padta hai, aur jab cache mein kuch nahi hota toh sirf root hi hai jo har TLD ka referral de sakta hai. Bina hints ke resolver ke paas pehla packet bhejne ka address hi nahi hoga -- chicken and egg.

src/root-hints.ts mein ROOT_HINTS ek readonly array hai, IANA/InterNIC ki named.root file se copy kiya hua ('last update: November 12, 2026'), source aur date comment mein likhe hain. Hard-coded list isliye theek hai kyunki yeh addresses bahut kam badalte hain (comment mein example: B root 2023 mein 170.247.170.2 par gaya), aur resolver ko shuru karne ke liye sirf EK reachable root chahiye -- poori list resilience ke liye hai.

closestServers() cache mein koi zone cut na mile toh hints ko servers bana deta hai: zone "" (root) aur har hint ka ipv4. Hints mein ipv6 bhi hai lekin resolver sirf IPv4 par bhejta hai. Tests FAKE_ROOT_HINTS (ek hi fake root, 198.51.100.1) inject karte hain, isliye internet nahi chahiye.

Honest point: real resolvers start-up par "priming" karte hain -- ek root se "." ka current NS set poochte hain taaki purani list bhi chal jaaye. Is project mein priming implement nahi hai (README NOT implemented list), hints seedhe use hote hain.
why_needed: Har iterative resolution ka anchor root hai; hints na ho toh resolver kuch bhi resolve nahi kar sakta.
real_world_analogy: Naye sheher mein aapke paas sirf ek purana phone directory ka pehla page hai jisme city enquiry ke numbers hain. Baaki sab wahi se pata chalega. Number kabhi kabhaar badalta hai, isliye smart log pehli call mein naya directory maang lete hain (priming).
how_it_works: Resolver constructor: this.hints = opts.rootHints ?? ROOT_HINTS. closestServers: koi cached NS + address nahi -> { zone: '', servers: hints.map(h => ({ name: h.name, ip: h.ipv4 })) }. askZone in servers ko (shuffled) ek ek karke try karta hai.
in_this_project: src/root-hints.ts: RootHint interface (name, ipv4, optional ipv6) aur ROOT_HINTS ke 13 entries. test/fixtures.ts: FAKE_ROOT_HINTS = [{ name: 'a.root-servers.test', ipv4: ROOT_IP }]. Live test 'a.root-servers.net A and AAAA: same as our own root hints, and the same as the OS resolver' hints ko asli duniya se match karta hai (README: 6/6 passed, opt-in LIVE_DNS=1).
advantages: Zero dependency start, koi bootstrap server nahi chahiye
Tests mein hints inject karke poora internet fake ho jaata hai
Source aur date likha hai, audit aasaan
disadvantages: List purani ho jaaye aur priming na ho toh kuch roots unreachable
IPv6 addresses ka use nahi hota
common_mistakes: Sochna ki 13 root servers = 13 machines (asal mein anycast, bahut saari)
Hints ko DNS se resolve karne ki koshish (chicken and egg)
Hints ko cache entry jaisa expire karna
follow_up_questions: Root priming kaise implement karoge is code mein?
Anycast root servers kaise kaam karte hain?
Agar saare hint addresses unreachable ho toh error kaisa dikhega?

question: What is a referral and a zone cut, and how does the resolver recognise a referral in a response?
answer_hinglish:
Zone cut woh jagah hai jahan DNS tree ki zimmedari ek server se doosre ko jaati hai. Root "test" zone ko delegate karta hai, test zone "alpha.test" ko. Jab hum root se www.alpha.test poochte hain, root answer nahi jaanta; woh referral deta hai: answer section khaali, authority section mein "test NS ns1.nic.test", aur additional mein us NS ka address (glue). Matlab "neeche wale zone ke servers yeh hain, unse poocho".

classify() mein referral pehchaanne ka logic: pehle check hota hai ki answer ya CNAME hai ya nahi. Dono nahi, toh authority ke NS records dekhe jaate hain; cut = pehle NS ka owner name. Agar cut us zone ke barabar nahi hai jisse humne poocha, toh yeh referral ho sakta hai -- lekin sirf tab jab cut humare zone ke strictly NEECHE ho aur hamara naam cut ke neeche ho (isSubdomain(cut, zone) && isSubdomain(name, cut)). Tab NS set referral rank par cache hota hai, glue nikala jaata hai, aur Outcome { kind: 'referral', zone: cut, hosts, glue } wapas jaata hai.

resolveOne() is outcome par zone = out.zone karta hai, serversFor() se naye servers laata hai, aur loop dobara askZone karta hai -- ek level neeche. Trace mein yeh line dikhti hai: 'referral . -> test (ns1.nic.test)', phir 'referral test -> alpha.test (ns1.alpha.test, ns2.alpha.test)'. Fixture test 'follows root -> test -> alpha.test referrals using glue' isi walk ko 3 queries mein prove karta hai.
why_needed: Referral samajhna hi iterative resolution ka dil hai; har step par resolver ko decide karna hai ki answer mila ya ek level aage jaana hai.
real_world_analogy: Sarkari daftar: aap main gate par poochte ho, guard bolta hai 'yeh department teesri manzil par hai, room 301 mein Sharma ji' -- woh khud answer nahi deta, sirf sahi jagah bhejta hai, aur room number (glue) bhi bata deta hai.
how_it_works: Server reply: AA=0, answers empty, authority = NS set of child zone, additional = A records of NS hosts. classify: answers check -> CNAME check -> NS in authority -> cut != zone -> downward check -> referral outcome. resolveOne loop maxReferrals tak chalta hai.
in_this_project: src/resolver.ts classify ka referral block; resolveOne ka loop 'for (let referrals = 0; referrals <= this.maxReferrals; referrals++)' aur trace 'referral ${zone || "."} -> ${out.zone}'. Fixture tree test/fixtures.ts ki top comment mein drawn hai (root -> test -> alpha.test, beta.test, loop1/loop2, lame).
advantages: Referral detection data-driven hai, AA bit par depend nahi
Downward check se upar/side mein bhejne wale broken servers turant pakde jaate hain
disadvantages: Sirf pehle NS owner (ns[0]) ko cut maana jaata hai; ajeeb mixed authority section ka koi special handling nahi
common_mistakes: Referral ko NODATA samajh lena (dono mein answers khaali hote hain)
Referral mein aaye NS ko answer rank par cache kar dena
Cut ka downward check bhool jaana
follow_up_questions: Referral aur NODATA response ko kaise alag karte ho?
Agar authority mein apne hi zone ka NS aaye (cut == zone) toh kya hota hai?

question: What is glue, what is the difference between in-bailiwick and out-of-bailiwick nameservers, and how does serversFor get the addresses of a new zone's servers?
answer_hinglish:
Glue woh A record hai jo parent zone referral ke saath additional section mein bhejta hai taaki hum naye zone ke NS host ko reach kar sakein. Zaroorat kyun: agar alpha.test ka NS ns1.alpha.test hai, toh ns1.alpha.test ka address alpha.test zone hi jaanta hai -- bina glue ke chicken and egg. Is case ko in-bailiwick NS kehte hain: NS host ka naam us zone ke andar hai jisne referral bheja, isliye parent ka glue maanna safe hai.

Out-of-bailiwick NS: beta.test ka NS ns.hoster.example hai, jo bilkul alag tree (example) mein hai. test TLD us naam ke baare mein authoritative nahi, isliye uska glue (agar bheje bhi) classify() drop kar deta hai -- glue sirf tab rakha jaata hai jab woh askZone wale zone ke andar ho (inZone) aur NS host set mein ho.

serversFor() teen jagah dekhta hai, is order mein: (1) is referral ka glue, (2) cache (cachedAddresses, referral rank ya upar), (3) nested lookup: har NS host ke liye resolveChain(host, A) depth + 1 ke saath, ek host ek baar mein. Pehla host jiske addresses mil gaye, wahi use hote hain. Agar ctx.depth >= maxDepth toh nested lookup hi nahi hota: ResolveError 'NS lookups nested deeper than ...'.

Test 'out-of-bailiwick NS without glue: resolves ns.hoster.example first, then asks it for beta.test' dikhata hai ki example TLD se ns.hoster.example poocha gaya, phir hoster server se pehle apna naam aur phir www.beta.test, aur trace mein 'no glue: resolving NS host ns.hoster.example' aaya.
why_needed: Real internet mein bahut saare domains apne DNS provider ke naam wale NS use karte hain (out-of-bailiwick). Resolver ko dono cases sahi handle karne hain, warna aadhe domains resolve hi nahi honge.
real_world_analogy: In-bailiwick: building ka guard bolta hai 'Sharma ji isi building ke room 301 mein hain' -- guard ko pata hai, maan lo. Out-of-bailiwick: guard bolta hai 'unka office doosri building mein hai, wahan ka address yeh hai' -- yeh guard ka area nahi, khud jaakar verify karo.
how_it_works: classify: glueRecords = additional.filter(inZone && type A && hostSet.has(name)) -> Map<host, ips[]>, referral rank par cache. serversFor: glue -> cachedAddresses -> depth check -> for host: resolveChain(host, TYPE.A, { budget: ctx.budget, depth: ctx.depth + 1 }); ResolveError par agla host; budget khatam toh break.
in_this_project: src/resolver.ts serversFor aur classify ka glue block. Fixtures: alpha.test (ns1/ns2.alpha.test, glue 192.0.2.1/.2) aur beta.test (ns.hoster.example, NO glue). Test 'bailiwick: out-of-zone glue in a referral is not used; the NS name is resolved properly' TLD se ns.hoster.example ka nakli glue 192.0.2.66 bhejta hai aur dikhata hai ki cache mein HOSTER_IP hi aaya.
advantages: Glue hone par zero extra queries
Out-of-bailiwick glue ignore hone se poisoning ka ek raasta band
Nested lookup wahi resolveChain reuse karta hai, alag code nahi
disadvantages: Out-of-bailiwick NS ke liye extra queries (beta.test test mein 3 extra)
NS hosts ek ek karke resolve hote hain, parallel nahi
AAAA glue use nahi hota (IPv4 only)
common_mistakes: Har glue record ko blindly trust karna
Nested lookup ko apna alag budget de dena
NS host ka naam case-sensitive compare karna (code toLowerCase karta hai)
follow_up_questions: Agar ns.hoster.example khud beta.test ke andar hota (ns.beta.test) aur glue na hota toh kya hota?
Sibling glue (test TLD dwara loop2 ka glue loop1 referral mein) kya safe hai?
NS host ek CNAME ho toh yeh code kya karega?

question: What is the difference between NXDOMAIN and NODATA, and why is an empty non-terminal NODATA and not NXDOMAIN?
answer_hinglish:
NXDOMAIN (rcode 3) ka matlab: yeh NAAM hi exist nahi karta, kisi bhi type ke liye. NODATA koi rcode nahi hai: rcode NOERROR hai, answer section khaali hai, authority mein zone ka SOA hai -- matlab naam exist karta hai lekin poocha gaya TYPE nahi hai. Example fixtures se: nope.alpha.test A -> NXDOMAIN; mail.alpha.test AAAA -> NODATA, kyunki mail.alpha.test ka A record hai, AAAA nahi.

Empty non-terminal: sub.alpha.test ka khud koi record nahi hai, lekin host.sub.alpha.test hai. DNS tree mein sub.alpha.test ek node hai jiske neeche kuch hai, isliye naam "exist" karta hai -- answer NODATA hona chahiye. Agar server NXDOMAIN de de, toh resolver ye maan sakta hai ki uske neeche bhi kuch nahi (RFC 8020 ka idea), aur host.sub.alpha.test bhi tod dega.

classify() mein: rcode NXDOMAIN aur koi CNAME nahi -> cache.putNegative(name, type, 'NXDOMAIN', soa) aur negative outcome. NOERROR, koi matching answer/CNAME/referral nahi -> NODATA: putNegative(name, type, 'NODATA', soa), rcode NOERROR. Cache mein farak important hai: NXDOMAIN poore naam ke liye (har type) cache hota hai, NODATA sirf us name + type ke liye.

Test 'NODATA: the name exists but not with this type (and an empty non-terminal is NODATA too)' dono cases check karta hai, aur 'NXDOMAIN comes back with the zone's SOA' dikhata hai ki authority[0] alpha.test ka SOA hai.
why_needed: Client ko sahi signal dena: NXDOMAIN par browser 'site does not exist' dikhata hai, NODATA par woh doosra type (A vs AAAA) try karta hai. Galat signal = toota hua dual-stack.
real_world_analogy: NXDOMAIN: 'is naam ka koi employee company mein hai hi nahi'. NODATA: 'haan, Sharma ji hain, par unka koi mobile number register nahi, sirf landline hai'. Empty non-terminal: 'Sales department mein khud koi nahi baitha, lekin uske andar teams hain' -- department exist karta hai.
how_it_works: Authoritative server: naam nahi mila aur uske neeche bhi kuch nahi -> NXDOMAIN + SOA. Naam ya uske neeche kuch hai, type nahi -> NOERROR + SOA. Resolver classify mein rcode aur sections dekh ke negative outcome banata hai, SOA ke saath RFC 2308 negative caching.
in_this_project: src/resolver.ts classify: NXDOMAIN branch aur aakhri NODATA branch ('NOERROR, nothing for our name, no referral: NODATA'). Fixture: test/fixtures.ts mein A('host.sub.alpha.test', '192.0.2.90') empty non-terminal banata hai; fake server 'exists = recs.some(r => isSubdomain(r.name, q.name))' se decide karta hai. Cache tests: 'NXDOMAIN is cached for the SOA minimum (60 s) and covers other types of the same name' aur 'NODATA is cached per type'.
advantages: Client ko sahi rcode milta hai
Negative caching se baar baar wahi missing naam upstream nahi jaata
disadvantages: NODATA ka koi alag rcode nahi, isliye 'NOERROR + empty' ko referral aur lame response se alag karna padta hai
common_mistakes: NODATA ko NXDOMAIN mein badal dena
NXDOMAIN ko sirf us type ke liye cache karna (mutation C4)
Empty non-terminal ko NXDOMAIN maan lena
follow_up_questions: NODATA response ka TTL kahan se aata hai?
Agar response mein SOA na ho toh negative entry cache hogi?
RFC 8020 NXDOMAIN-cut kya hai?

question: Walk through resolveOne: in what order does it check the cache, and how does the referral loop work?
answer_hinglish:
resolveOne(name, type, ctx) CNAME chain ke ek link ko resolve karta hai aur ek Outcome lautata hai. Pehle teen cache checks, is order mein:

1. getRRset(name, type, 'answer') -- positive answer cached hai? Seedha answer. Dhyan do: minRank 'answer' hai, isliye referral se seekha glue kabhi client answer nahi banta.
2. getNegative(name, type) -- NXDOMAIN ya NODATA cached? Negative outcome, SOA ke saath.
3. Agar type CNAME nahi hai: getRRset(name, CNAME, 'answer') -- cached alias? cname outcome; resolveChain target follow karega. Mutation R11 ('cached CNAME not followed') isi check ko todta tha.

Order ka logic: exact answer sabse specific hai; negative usse pehle aata hai jo hum upstream bhejte; CNAME check type CNAME ke liye skip, kyunki tab CNAME record khud answer hai.

Phir network: closestServers(name) sabse gehra known zone cut deta hai (warna root). Loop: askZone(zone, servers, name, type, ctx). Outcome referral nahi hai (answer, cname, negative) toh return. Referral hai toh trace line, zone = out.zone, servers = await serversFor(out.hosts, out.glue, ctx), aur agla round. Loop 'referrals <= maxReferrals' tak chalta hai; usse zyada ho toh ResolveError 'more than 16 referrals for ...' (default 16). Lame outcome yahan kabhi nahi aata: askZone usse next server mein convert kar deta hai, aur saare fail ho toh throw.

Isliye cold lookup www.alpha.test = 3 askZone calls (root, test, alpha.test); warm sibling mail.alpha.test = closestServers seedha alpha.test deta hai, 1 query.
why_needed: Yeh function cache aur network ke beech ka glue hai; interviewer yahi trace karwata hai: 'pehla packet kab jaata hai?'.
real_world_analogy: Library mein kitaab dhoondhna: pehle apni shelf (answer), phir 'yeh kitaab exist nahi karti' wali list (negative), phir 'yeh kitaab doosre naam se hai' card (CNAME). Kuch nahi mila toh sabse nazdeeki section se shuru karke counter se counter jaana (referrals).
how_it_works: Ctx { budget, depth } poore resolve() mein share hota hai. Loop har iteration mein ek zone ke servers ko poochta hai; referral zone ko ek level neeche le jaata hai; serversFor glue/cache/nested lookup se IPs laata hai.
in_this_project: src/resolver.ts resolveOne. Tests: 'a second lookup is answered from the cache, and a sibling name starts at the cached zone cut' (0 queries, phir 1 query, root ko kuch nahi), cache.test.ts ka 'a cached CNAME is followed without asking again' (R11 pakadne wala).
advantages: Cache-first, warm lookups 0 queries
Referral loop simple aur bounded
Outcome union se har case explicit
disadvantages: Har link ke liye closestServers dobara chalta hai (cheap, lekin repeated)
Referral loop sequential, koi parallel exploration nahi
common_mistakes: Negative check CNAME check ke baad rakhna ya bhool jaana
TYPE CNAME query par bhi cached CNAME ko follow kar dena
Referral loop ko unbounded chhod dena
follow_up_questions: maxReferrals limit ka koi test hai? Kaise likhoge?
Agar cache mein answer hai lekin TTL 1 second bacha hai toh kya karoge (prefetch)?

question: In what order does classify interpret a response, and why does that order matter?
answer_hinglish:
classify(reply, zone, name, type) ek server ke response ko ek Outcome mein badalta hai, aur jo rakha jaata hai use wahin cache karta hai. Order:

1. Bailiwick filter: inZone = class IN aur isSubdomain(rr.name, zone). Bahar wale records 'dropped N out-of-bailiwick record(s)' trace ke saath gin ke chhod diye jaate hain; answers = reply.answers.filter(inZone). SOA bhi zone ke andar aur naam ke upar hona chahiye.
2. rcode NXDOMAIN: agar answers mein hamare naam ka CNAME hai toh cname outcome (alias exist karta hai, target nahi), warna NXDOMAIN negative.
3. Direct answer: type match aur sameName(name). Poora answers section RRsets mein group karke answer rank par cache.
4. CNAME for name: cname outcome (caller target follow karega).
5. Authority mein NS aur cut != zone: downward check -> referral, warna lame.
6. Kuch nahi: AA=0 aur SOA nahi -> lame ('empty non-authoritative response'); warna NODATA.

Order kyun matter karta hai: answer aur CNAME referral se pehle check hote hain, kyunki bahut servers answer ke saath authority mein NS bhi bhejte hain -- agar referral pehle dekhte toh answer ko referral samajh lete. NXDOMAIN sabse pehle isliye ki NXDOMAIN response mein answer ho hi nahi sakta (sirf CNAME). Lame check NODATA se pehle: ek non-authoritative khaali response ko NODATA maan ke cache karna galat negative cache hai. Aur bailiwick filter sabse pehle, taaki neeche ka koi branch out-of-zone record ko dekh hi na sake.

Ek subtle baat: askZone rcode check classify se pehle karta hai -- sirf NOERROR aur NXDOMAIN classify tak pahunchte hain; SERVFAIL/REFUSED/FORMERR next server.
why_needed: Ek response mein ek saath answer, authority NS, additional glue sab ho sakte hain; galat order = galat outcome = poisoned ya galat cache.
real_world_analogy: Post sorting: pehle check karo letter isi pin code ka hai ya nahi (bailiwick), phir 'addressee not found' stamp (NXDOMAIN), phir seedha delivery (answer), phir 'naya address' sticker (CNAME), phir 'doosre post office bhejo' (referral). Order ulta karo toh letter galat jagah jaayega.
how_it_works: Har branch ek Outcome lautati hai; caching branch ke andar hoti hai: answers -> cacheAnswers (answer rank), referral NS + glue -> putRRset(.., 'referral'), negative -> putNegative. Lame kuch cache nahi karta.
in_this_project: src/resolver.ts classify ki doc comment: 'Everything outside zone is dropped here (bailiwick), and everything that is kept is cached here.' Tests jo har branch chhoote hain: alias (answer + CNAME ek response mein), NXDOMAIN, NODATA, lame test, bailiwick tests ('dropped 3 out-of-bailiwick'). Mutations R2 (filter off), R6 (lame check off), R7 (glue answer rank) sab pakde gaye.
advantages: Ek hi jagah filter + interpret + cache, audit aasaan
Har branch ka apna test aur mutation
Pure function jaisa (reply, zone) -> outcome, sirf cache side effect
disadvantages: Cache side effects classify ke andar, isliye 'sirf dekhna' mumkin nahi
Sirf ns[0] ka owner cut maana jaata hai
common_mistakes: Referral ko answer se pehle check karna
Bailiwick filter ko answers par lagana lekin glue par nahi
Non-authoritative empty response ko NODATA maan lena
follow_up_questions: Agar answer mein hamara record bhi ho aur authority mein child zone ka NS bhi, toh?
classify ko pure banane ke liye kya refactor karoge?
AA bit ko kahan use kiya hai aur kahan jaan boojh kar nahi?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Interpret aur cache ek function mein hai -- simple, lekin test mein side-effect-free check mushkil. Alternative: classify sirf Outcome + 'records to cache' list lautaye, caller cache kare.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Galat order ka asli failure: answer ke saath aaya apex NS referral samjha jaata (cut == zone wala check isse bachata hai), ya lame empty response NODATA ban ke ghanton cache ho jaata.
advanced.alternatives: Unbound/BIND jaise resolvers response type ko pehle classify karte hain (ANSWER, CNAME, REFERRAL, NODATA, NXDOMAIN, LAME) phir alag 'scrubber' step chalta hai; yahan wahi idea ek function mein hai.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Traffic badhne se classify ki logic nahi badalti; per-response cost records ki ginti par linear hai. Badi scale par asli farak cache size aur scrubbing ke detailed rules (RFC 2181 ranking ke saare levels) mein aata hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Scrubber ko alag function banana, poori RFC 2181 5.4.1 ranking, CNAME + NXDOMAIN non-final zone handling (README NOT implemented), aur DNSSEC validation ke liye hook.

question: How does closestServers find the best zone cut to start from, and why does it need both the NS set and an address?
answer_hinglish:
closestServers(name) naam se upar ki taraf chalta hai -- www.alpha.test, phir alpha.test, phir test -- aur pehla ancestor lautata hai jiska NS set cache mein hai AUR jiske kam se kam ek NS host ka A record cache mein hai. Kuch na mile toh root hints. Sabse gehra (deepest) cut isliye ki woh name ke sabse kareeb hai: alpha.test pata hai toh root aur test ko poochna bekaar hai.

Dono kyun chahiye: sirf NS set se kaam nahi chalta, NS ek naam hai, packet bhejne ke liye IP chahiye. Agar NS set cached hai lekin uske hosts ke addresses expire ho gaye, toh woh cut use nahi kar sakte -- isliye loop 'servers.length' check karta hai aur nahi toh ek level upar jaata hai. Yeh fallback safe hai: parent zone fir se referral + glue dega.

Lookup minRank 'referral' ke saath hota hai: getRRset(zone, NS, 'referral') aur cachedAddresses mein getRRset(host, A, 'referral'). Matlab referral se seekha data (low rank) zone cut dhoondhne ke liye use hota hai, bhale hi client ko answer mein kabhi na diya jaaye. Yeh ranking ka do-tarafa use hai.

Effect test mein dikhta hai: 'a sibling name starts at the cached zone cut' -- mail.alpha.test 1 query mein, root ko zero. Aur cache.test.ts ka 'an answer is re-fetched after its TTL (300 s), but the zone cut (86400 s) is still used': www.alpha.test ka A 300 s mein expire, lekin alpha.test NS (86400 s TTL) cached hai, isliye refetch 1 query, root nahi.
why_needed: Iske bina har lookup root se shuru hota -- root servers par load, har lookup mein 2 extra round trips. Zone cut caching hi resolver ko fast banata hai.
real_world_analogy: Kisi office mein file le jaani hai: agar aapko pata hai ki file Accounts ke room 204 mein jaati hai aur room 204 ka raasta bhi yaad hai, toh seedhe wahi jaoge. Sirf naam yaad hai, raasta bhool gaye -- toh ek level upar reception se dobara poochoge.
how_it_works: for zone = canonicalName(name); zone !== ''; zone = parentName(zone): NS RRset (referral rank+) -> host names -> cachedAddresses -> non-empty toh return. Labels jitne iterations, har ek cache Map lookup.
in_this_project: src/resolver.ts closestServers aur cachedAddresses. Comment: 'The deepest ancestor of name whose NS set and at least one NS address are cached; the root otherwise.' Test names: 'a second lookup is answered from the cache, and a sibling name starts at the cached zone cut', cache.test.ts 'an answer is re-fetched after its TTL (300 s), but the zone cut (86400 s) is still used'.

Address expire ho toh apne aap ek level upar fallback
Simple loop, labels ki ginti tak
disadvantages: Out-of-bailiwick NS jinke address cached nahi, unka cut skip ho jaata hai aur parent se dobara referral aata hai (kuch extra queries)
Root ka khud ka NS set cache se nahi aata, hamesha hints
common_mistakes: Sirf NS set dekh ke cut chun lena, address check bhoolna
Shallowest match lena (root ke paas wala)
Answer rank ka NS hi maanna aur referral rank ignore karna
follow_up_questions: closestServers ko root ke liye bhi cache use karna ho (priming) toh kya badlega?
Agar NS set cached hai aur hosts out-of-bailiwick hain bina cached address ke, toh lookup kaise aage badhta hai?

question: How is the resolution algorithm split into resolve, resolveChain, resolveOne, askZone, exchange and classify, and why this layering?
answer_hinglish:
Har layer ek hi sawaal ka jawab deti hai:

- resolve(name, type): public API. Ek naya Ctx ({ budget: { queries: 0 }, depth: 0 }) banata hai, aur ResolveError/WireError ko SERVFAIL Resolution mein badalta hai (reason ke saath). Baaki errors bugs hain, unhe upar fenk deta hai.
- resolveChain: CNAME chain -- maxCnameChain tak links, har link ke CNAME records answers mein jodta hai.
- resolveOne: ek naam ka ek link -- cache checks, closestServers, referral loop (maxReferrals).
- serversFor: naye zone ke server IPs -- glue, cache, nested lookup (maxDepth).
- askZone: ek zone ke servers ek ek karke, budget check (maxQueries), timeout/SERVFAIL/REFUSED/lame par next server.
- exchange: ek server se ek query, UDP, TC par usi server se TCP.
- classify: ek response -> Outcome, bailiwick filter aur caching.

Fayda: har limit apni sahi layer par hai aur alag test hota hai: CNAME limit resolveChain mein, referral limit resolveOne mein, depth serversFor mein, budget askZone mein. Outcome discriminated union (answer, cname, negative, referral, lame) se layers ke beech contract explicit hai; TypeScript batata hai agar koi kind handle nahi kiya.

Recursion bhi saaf hai: serversFor nested lookup ke liye wapas resolveChain bulata hai, depth + 1 aur SAME budget object ke saath. Isliye ek lookup ke andar chahe kitni nested lookups ho, total queries maxQueries par bounded hai. transport.ts (spoofing checks) aur cache.ts (TTL, ranking) resolver ke bahar hain; resolver unhe sirf call karta hai, isliye tests route hook se fake network laga lete hain.
why_needed: Senior interview mein yahi dekhte hain ki tum ek protocol algorithm ko testable, bounded layers mein tod sakte ho ya ek 500-line function likhte ho.
real_world_analogy: Courier company: front desk (resolve) order leta hai aur complaint ka jawab deta hai, route planner (resolveChain/resolveOne) decide karta hai kaunsa hub, hub manager (askZone) us hub ke delivery boys ko ek ek karke bhejta hai, delivery boy (exchange) ek ghar jaata hai, aur sorting clerk (classify) wapas aaye parcel ko check karta hai.
how_it_works: resolve -> resolveChain -> resolveOne -> [closestServers] -> askZone -> exchange -> classify -> Outcome; referral par serversFor -> (nested) resolveChain. Errors: ResolveError upar tak, resolve() par SERVFAIL.
in_this_project: src/resolver.ts ki top comment poora algorithm likhti hai. Ctx interface, Outcome type, ResolveError class. Tests: test/resolver.test.ts ke 4 describe blocks (walking down from the root; CNAME, NXDOMAIN, NODATA; TCP fallback and failing servers; spoofing and cache-poisoning defences) layers ko bahar se chalate hain.
advantages: Har limit ki ek jagah, ek test
Outcome union se exhaustive handling
Transport aur cache inject ho sakte hain (route, cache option)
Nested lookup code reuse, alag implementation nahi
disadvantages: Private methods sirf public resolve() se test hote hain
Ctx manually pass karna padta hai har layer mein
common_mistakes: Budget ko har nested lookup mein naya bana dena
Har error ko SERVFAIL mein nigal jaana (yahan sirf ResolveError/WireError, baaki bugs dikhte hain)
Transport aur resolver logic mix karna
follow_up_questions: Is design mein QNAME minimisation kis layer mein jaayega?
In-flight dedupe kis layer par lagaoge?
Resolver ko state machine (event driven) mein kyun ya kyun nahi likhoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Async/await recursive design padhne mein seedha hai; Unbound jaisa event-driven state machine zyada scalable hai (hazaron in-flight queries, ek thread) lekin samajhna mushkil. Node ka event loop yahan concurrency khud deta hai, isliye recursive async kaafi hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar koi naya error type (jaise socket EMFILE) ResolveError nahi hai toh resolve() use rethrow karega aur server ko handle karna padega -- yeh jaan boojh kar hai taaki bugs SERVFAIL ke peeche na chhupein.
advanced.alternatives: Ek bada loop with explicit stack (iterative state machine); ya forwarding-only design jisme in mein se aadhi layers hoti hi nahi.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x/100x traffic par layering wahi rehti hai; jo jodna padega: in-flight dedupe (resolve level), server RTT/health memory (askZone level), cache size/LRU (cache.ts), aur multiple processes ke beech shared cache.
advanced.production_improvements: Har layer ke metrics (queries per resolve, referrals, nested depth, timeouts per server), prefetch, serve-stale, QNAME minimisation, DNSSEC -- sab README ke NOT implemented list mein hain.

question: Treating the cache as the resolver's database of delegations, how are NS sets and glue stored, keyed and ranked, and how does the resolver query them?
answer_hinglish:
Resolver ke liye cache sirf answers ka store nahi, delegations ka database bhi hai. Data model: key = (lowercased name, type), value = poora RRset (saare records ek saath), expiry = RRset ka sabse chhota TTL, aur har entry ka ek rank: 'referral' ya 'answer'.

Referral mein jo aata hai -- child zone ka NS set (authority) aur in-zone glue A records (additional) -- woh classify() mein putRRset(.., 'referral') se rakha jaata hai. Glue pehle groupRRsets() se (name, type) groups mein banta hai, kyunki cache whole RRsets store karta hai, single records nahi. Answers cacheAnswers() se 'answer' rank par.

Query patterns do hain, aur rank ek tarah ka access control hai:
- Client answer: resolveOne getRRset(name, type, 'answer') -- referral rank data yahan invisible hai. Test 'referral data (NS and glue) is cached at low rank: never returned as an answer' prove karta hai ki ns1.alpha.test ka glue cache mein hai lekin answer ke liye authority se dobara poocha jaata hai.
- Delegation lookup: closestServers/cachedAddresses getRRset(.., 'referral') -- yahan dono ranks chalte hain.

Write rule: referral data ek unexpired answer ko overwrite nahi kar sakta (mutation C5). Isse ek parent ka purana glue child ke authoritative answer ko nahi badal sakta.

TTL hi expiry hai: alpha.test NS 86400 s par aaya, www ka A 300 s par, isliye A expire hone ke baad bhi cut zinda hai. Negative entries bhi isi store mein: NXDOMAIN per name, NODATA per name+type, SOA minimum se TTL.
why_needed: Delegation data ko galat rank ya galat key par rakha toh ya toh har lookup root se shuru hoga, ya glue client answer ban ke poisoning ka raasta khulega.
real_world_analogy: Ek company directory jisme do tarah ki entries hain: HR ki verified entries (answer) aur 'reception ne bataya tha' wali pencil entries (referral). Raasta dhoondhne ke liye pencil entry chalegi, lekin kisi ko officially number dena ho toh sirf verified entry.
how_it_works: putRRset(rrs, rank): key name|type, TTL = min, capped maxTtl, TTL 0 skip, lower rank existing higher-rank unexpired ko overwrite nahi karta. getRRset(name, type, minRank): rank kam ho toh undefined; TTL count down karke copies lautata hai.
in_this_project: src/cache.ts: Rank type ('referral' | 'answer'), RANK_ORDER, putRRset, getRRset, putNegative. src/resolver.ts classify mein putRRset(nsSet, 'referral') aur glue groups; closestServers mein 'referral' minRank. README mutations R7 (glue answer rank) aur C5/C6 sab pakde gaye.
advantages: Ek hi store se answers aur delegations
Rank se poisoning-resistant writes
RRset granularity DNS semantics se match
disadvantages: Sirf do ranks; RFC 2181 ke saare levels nahi
Eviction oldest-first, LRU nahi (README)
common_mistakes: Glue ko answer ki tarah cache karna
Records ko individually store karna aur RRset todna
Key mein case-sensitive naam
follow_up_questions: NS set ka TTL parent ne diya aur child ne alag diya -- kaunsa jeetna chahiye?
Redis jaise shared store mein yeh model kaise map karoge?

question: Inside one resolution, the Ctx budget is shared by reference with nested lookups while depth is copied. Why, and what state is shared between concurrent resolve() calls?
answer_hinglish:
Node single-threaded hai, isliye 'concurrency' yahan interleaving hai: har resolve() async hai aur har await (ek UDP query) par doosra resolve() chal sakta hai. Shared cheez sirf Cache hai (Resolver.cache); har resolve() ka apna Ctx hota hai -- apna budget aur depth. Cache ke methods synchronous hain, isliye do awaits ke beech ek putRRset beech mein toota nahi ja sakta; data race jaisa koi corruption nahi.

Ek resolve() ke andar sab sequential hai: askZone servers ek ek karke, serversFor NS hosts ek ek karke. Koi parallel query nahi, isliye budget ki ginti simple hai.

Budget aur depth ka farak jaan boojh kar hai. serversFor nested lookup ko naya Ctx deta hai: { budget: ctx.budget, depth: ctx.depth + 1 }. depth ek number hai -- copy hota hai, kyunki woh PATH-local sawaal hai: 'yeh branch kitni gehri hai'. Nested lookup se wapas aane par parent ki depth wahi rehti hai. budget ek object hai -- reference share hota hai, kyunki woh RESOLUTION-global sawaal hai: 'is client query ne total kitna kaam karwaya'. Agar budget bhi copy hota, toh har nested level ko phir se 60 queries milti aur delegation fan-out multiply ho jaata. Isi wajah se serversFor nested call ke baad 'ctx.budget.queries >= this.maxQueries' check kar sakta hai: child ka kharch parent ko dikhta hai.

Concurrent resolve() calls ke beech budget share NAHI hota (har resolve() naya Ctx), isliye ek heavy client doosre ka budget nahi khaata. In-flight dedupe nahi hai (README), us par alag sawaal hai.

Shared cache ka side effect: ek resolution ka seekha zone cut doosri ko agle closestServers call par turant dikhta hai.
why_needed: Stub server (src/server.ts) har client query par resolve() bulata hai; load par concurrent behaviour hi decide karta hai ki upstream par kitna traffic jaayega.
real_world_analogy: Ek office mein 10 log ek hi file maang rahe hain. Abhi har banda khud record room jaata hai (no dedupe). Better: pehla banda jaaye, baaki uske laut ne ka intezaar karein aur photocopy le lein.
how_it_works: Event loop: resolve A -> await queryUdp -> resolve B chalta hai -> ... Cache Map synchronous updates. Ctx per resolve; budget object nested lookups mein shared by reference.
in_this_project: src/resolver.ts: Ctx interface, resolve() mein naya Ctx, serversFor mein budget sharing. README NOT implemented: 'No in-flight deduplication: two identical concurrent queries both go upstream.' Test 'query IDs and source ports are random' 20 resolutions chalata hai (sequentially, await ke saath).
advantages: Single thread: cache par locks nahi chahiye
Per-resolve budget: ek client ki query doosre ka budget nahi khaati
Sequential server tries se upstream par halka load
disadvantages: No dedupe: cold cache par thundering herd
Sequential tries: dead server ki poori timeout latency
Ek process ka cache doosre process se share nahi
common_mistakes: Sochna ki async ka matlab parallel threads aur locks chahiye
Budget ko global (resolver-wide) bana dena -- ek heavy client sabko starve karega
Dedupe map se entry delete karna bhool jaana (failure par hamesha wahi error)
follow_up_questions: Agar serversFor NS hosts ko parallel resolve kare toh shared budget mein kya race aa sakti hai?
Multiple Node processes (cluster) mein cache share karoge ya nahi?
Parallel queries to two servers (hedged requests) kab worth it hain?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Sequential design simple aur upstream-friendly hai lekin tail latency kharab; parallel fan-out latency kam karta hai lekin upstream load aur budget accounting complex.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Cold cache par traffic spike: N identical resolutions, N guna upstream queries; ek slow server par saari queue ek saath ruk jaati hai.
advanced.alternatives: In-flight dedupe map; per-zone request coalescing; Unbound jaisa 'mesh' jahan ek query state ko kai clients subscribe karte hain.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x clients par dedupe zaroori ho jaata hai; 100x par ek process kam padega -- multiple processes ya machines, har ek ka apna cache (ya shared cache), aur upstream rate limiting.
advanced.production_improvements: Dedupe map, per-server concurrency limit, resolve() par overall deadline, aur metrics: in-flight count, queries per resolve, cache hit ratio.

question: How many upstream queries does a lookup cost in this resolver, cold and warm, and where does latency come from?
answer_hinglish:
Cost Resolution.queries mein seedha dikhta hai (har askZone attempt ek count). Fixture numbers, test se: cold www.alpha.test = 3 queries (root, test, alpha.test, glue ke saath). Wahi naam dobara = 0 (poora cache se). Sibling mail.alpha.test = 1 (zone cut cached). www.beta.test cold = 6 (code trace se; test sirf servers ke logs check karta hai) kyunki NS out-of-bailiwick hai: root, test, phir nested ns.hoster.example ke liye root, example, hoster, aur aakhir mein hoster se www.beta.test. NXDOMAIN for a missing TLD = 1 (root hi bol deta hai). Real internet par README ka www.wikipedia.org trace 5 queries ka hai, CNAME ke baad org NS cached hone se root skip hua.

Latency ke sources: (1) round trips -- cold lookup mein har level ek RTT; (2) timeouts -- askZone sequential hai, ek dead server pehle aaya toh poora timeoutMs (default 2000) intezaar, phir agla. README seedha kehta hai: 'a dead server costs a full timeout on every lookup that picks it first', kyunki dead servers yaad nahi rakhe jaate; (3) TC=1 par same server se TCP retry -- ek extra round trip plus TCP handshake, aur EDNS(0) nahi bhejte isliye 512 byte se bade answers hamesha TCP par jaate hain; (4) nested NS lookups.

Scale ke liye sabse bada lever cache hit ratio hai: long-TTL zone cuts (TLD NS typically 1-2 din) ki wajah se zyada tar lookups 1 query ya 0 par aate hain. README mein koi latency numbers claim nahi hain ('a handful of manual runs is not a measurement'), isliye main bhi numbers nahi dunga -- sirf query counts, jo tests assert karte hain.
why_needed: Interviewer performance ko 'kitne round trips aur kitne timeouts' mein sochna chahta hai; DNS latency seedhe har web request ki latency mein judti hai.
real_world_analogy: Pehli baar kisi naye mohalle mein address dhoondhna: teen logon se poochna padta hai. Doosri baar seedha ghar. Aur agar raaste mein koi aadmi so raha hai (dead server) toh uske jaagne ka intezaar (timeout) karke phir doosre se poochte ho.
how_it_works: queries = ctx.budget.queries (nested included). askZone har server try par ++ karta hai. Timeout: queryUdp timeoutMs. TC: exchange mein queryTcp. Cache: answers aur zone cuts.
in_this_project: Tests: 'follows root -> test -> alpha.test ...' (queries 3), 'a second lookup is answered from the cache ...' (0, phir 1), 'NXDOMAIN from the root for a TLD that does not exist' (1), 'a server that never answers times out and the next server of the zone is tried' (>= 190 ms with timeoutMs 200). README trace aur NOT implemented: RTT-based selection, EDNS(0), prefetch.

console.log(`\n;; ${rcodeName(r.rcode)}, ${r.queries} upstream queries, ${Date.now() - started} ms${r.reason ? ` (${r.reason})` : ""}`);

Zone cut caching se warm lookups sasti
Budget se worst case bounded
disadvantages: Dead server har baar poori timeout khaata hai
EDNS nahi, isliye bade answers par extra TCP round trip
Out-of-bailiwick NS par cold lookup do guna
common_mistakes: Latency numbers bina measurement ke claim karna
Sochna ki timeout sirf ek baar lagta hai (memory nahi hai, har lookup par)
Cache hit ratio ignore karke sirf code speed dekhna
follow_up_questions: Dead servers ko yaad rakhne ke liye kya data structure rakhoge?
Prefetch (TTL khatam hone se pehle refresh) kab worth it hai?
EDNS(0) jodne se query count par kya asar hoga?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Simple random order vs RTT tracking: random fair aur simple, RTT tracking fast lekin state rakhni padti hai aur stale ho sakti hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Ek zone ke do mein se ek server dead: lagbhag aadhi cold lookups 2 s slow (shuffle par depend). Saare dead: har ek ko ek try, phir SERVFAIL -- 'every server of a zone dead' test.
advanced.alternatives: Parallel queries to 2 servers, RTT-based selection (Unbound style smoothed RTT), shorter adaptive timeouts, EDNS(0) for bigger UDP.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x traffic par same names ka cache hit ratio aur badhega; 100x par in-flight dedupe aur multi-process caching chahiye, warna cold misses par upstream burst.
advanced.production_improvements: Per-server RTT/health table, adaptive timeouts, EDNS(0), prefetch, serve-stale (RFC 8767), latency histograms -- sab NOT implemented, README mein listed.

question: How do maxQueries, maxDepth and maxReferrals protect the resolver against malicious or broken delegations?
answer_hinglish:
Ek resolver doosron ke likhe zones follow karta hai, isliye attacker zone aise bana sakta hai ki resolver bahut kaam kare: delegation loops (loop1.test ka NS loop2.test mein, loop2.test ka loop1.test mein), bahut saare NS names bina glue ke jinhe har ek ko resolve karna pade, ya lambi referral chains. Research mein 'NXNSAttack' (2020) isi ka example tha: ek referral mein bahut saare glueless NS names, aur resolver har ek ke liye nested lookups karta hai -- ek client query, sau upstream queries. Isse resolver khud ek amplification weapon ban jaata hai.

Teen alag limits, teen alag dimensions:
- maxQueries (default 60): ek resolve() ke saare upstream queries, nested lookups samet. askZone har query se pehle check karta hai. Yeh total work ka hard cap hai.
- maxDepth (default 4): nested NS-address lookups kitne gehre. serversFor check karta hai. Yeh recursion ka cap hai, taaki loop1 <-> loop2 jaisa chakkar ruke.
- maxReferrals (default 16): ek lookup mein kitne referrals. resolveOne ka loop. Comment kehta hai: naam mein max 127 labels, real chains 3-5 deep.

Ek limit kaafi kyun nahi: budget akela work rokta hai lekin galat reason deta hai; depth akela recursion rokta hai lekin ek level par bahut saare NS hosts ka fan-out nahi. serversFor ek host ek baar mein try karta hai aur 'if (ctx.budget.queries >= this.maxQueries) break' se budget khatam hote hi ruk jaata hai.

Test 'a delegation loop without glue (loop1.test <-> loop2.test) ends in SERVFAIL, within the budget' plus R8/R9 ke liye alag tests. Honest: rate limiting per client is project mein nahi hai.
why_needed: Bina limits ke ek akela malicious domain resolver ka CPU, sockets aur upstream bandwidth kha sakta hai, aur use doosre servers par attack karne ke liye use kar sakta hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek delivery boy ko bola 'yeh parcel deliver karo'. Har ghar wala bolta hai 'agle ghar jao'. Limits: din mein 60 ghar se zyada nahi (budget), kisi ke kehne par 'pehle uska address pata karo' wala chakkar 4 level se zyada nahi (depth), aur 16 baar aage bhejne ke baad wapas (referrals).
how_it_works: Ctx.budget shared object; askZone: if (budget.queries >= maxQueries) throw; serversFor: if (depth >= maxDepth) throw; resolveOne: for referrals <= maxReferrals. Sab ResolveError -> resolve() mein SERVFAIL + reason.
in_this_project: src/resolver.ts ResolverOptions comments (default 60, 4, 16), askZone, serversFor, resolveOne. Fixtures: NS('loop1.test', 'ns.loop2.test'), NS('loop2.test', 'ns.loop1.test') bina glue. Tests: delegation loop test (maxQueries 40), 'the query budget alone: maxQueries 2 cannot finish a 3-query lookup', 'the nesting limit alone: maxDepth 0 forbids the nested NS lookup that beta.test needs'.
advantages: Har resolve() ka worst case bounded
Teen limits teen alag reasons dete hain, debugging aasaan
Limits options se configurable, tests chhote numbers use karte hain
disadvantages: Legit lekin bahut complex domains (lambi CNAME + out-of-bailiwick chains) bhi SERVFAIL ho sakte hain
Per-client rate limiting nahi, toh attacker bahut saari queries bhej ke phir bhi load bana sakta hai
Fan-out ka koi alag cap nahi (kitne NS hosts per referral), sirf budget
common_mistakes: Sirf ek limit lagana aur maanna ki loop ruk gaya
Nested lookup ko naya budget de dena
Limit hit hone par hang ya crash, SERVFAIL nahi
follow_up_questions: NXNSAttack ke against aur kya lagaoge (NS hosts per referral cap)?
Budget ke liye time-based deadline kyun nahi?
Stub server par per-client rate limiting kahan jodoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Tight limits = safer lekin kuch real domains fail; loose limits = sab chalta hai lekin attack surface bada. Defaults (60/4/16/8) BIND/Unbound jaise resolvers ke typical order ke hain, exact copy nahi.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Budget nested lookup mein khatam ho toh reason 'no address found for any NS host' aata hai, 'budget' nahi -- serversFor ResolveError pakad ke agla host try karta hai aur phir apna error deta hai. Debug karte waqt yeh confuse kar sakta hai.
advanced.alternatives: Per-referral NS fan-out cap (NXNSAttack mitigation jaisa resolvers ne kiya), time-based deadline per resolution, per-client query rate limits, response rate limiting.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada clients par limits per resolution kaafi nahi; total upstream rate aur per-client quotas chahiye, warna limit ke andar rehte hue bhi bahut saari queries kaafi load hain.
advanced.production_improvements: Fan-out cap, overall deadline, per-client rate limiting, metrics: kitni resolutions kis limit se ruki (budget/depth/referrals/CNAME).

question: What happens when a nameserver times out, returns SERVFAIL or REFUSED, or when every server of a zone is dead?
answer_hinglish:
Short answer: ek server ka failure lookup ka failure nahi hai; askZone usi zone ke agle server par jaata hai. Sirf jab saare servers fail ho jaayein tab ResolveError, jo resolve() mein SERVFAIL ban jaata hai.

askZone ke loop mein teen failure paths hain:
1. Transport error: exchange() TimeoutError, TransportError ya WireError fenke toh trace line, failures list mein '<ip>: TimeoutError', aur continue. Dhyan do: transport.ts galat/spoofed replies ko ignore karke wait karta rehta hai, isliye 'garbage reply' bhi aakhir mein timeout hi banta hai.
2. Bura rcode: NOERROR ya NXDOMAIN ke alawa kuch bhi (SERVFAIL, REFUSED, FORMERR, NOTIMP) -> '<server>: SERVFAIL, next server' aur continue. Mutation R5 (SERVFAIL accept kar lena) test ne pakda.
3. Lame: classify ne { kind: 'lame' } diya -> next server.

Saare try ho gaye: 'all servers for zone "alpha.test" failed (192.0.2.1: TimeoutError; 192.0.2.2: TimeoutError)'. Har server ko EK hi try milta hai -- koi retry loop nahi -- isliye worst case = servers x timeoutMs, aur budget bhi har try par ghatta hai.

Tests: 'a server that never answers times out and the next server of the zone is tried' (ALPHA1 drop, ALPHA2 answer, time >= 190 ms with timeoutMs 200), 'SERVFAIL or REFUSED from one server: the next one is tried', 'every server of a zone dead: SERVFAIL after one try each, not a hang' (har server ka log length 1), aur 'a garbage reply from the right server is ignored and the query times out to the next server'. Mutation R4 (timeout = lookup fail) ko 3 tests ne pakda.
why_needed: Real zones mein 2-13 servers isi liye hote hain ki ek down ho toh doosra kaam kare. Resolver ko us redundancy ka fayda uthana aana chahiye.
real_world_analogy: Bank ke teen counters hain. Pehla counter band hai (timeout) ya bolta hai 'aaj system down hai' (SERVFAIL) -- aap ghar nahi jaate, agle counter par jaate ho. Teeno band ho tabhi 'aaj kaam nahi hoga'.
how_it_works: for s of shuffled(servers): budget check -> exchange -> catch transport errors -> rcode check -> classify -> lame check -> return. Loop khatam -> throw ResolveError with failures joined.

question: What is a lame delegation or an upward referral, and how does the resolver detect and handle it?
answer_hinglish:
Lame delegation: parent ne kaha 'lame.test ke server ns.lame.test hai', lekin woh server lame.test ke liye sahi jawab nahi deta -- ya toh woh zone serve hi nahi karta, ya galat jagah refer karta hai. Sabse common khatarnak shape upward referral hai: server bolta hai 'root se poocho' (authority mein '. NS a.root-servers...') -- yeh hamein UPAR bhejta hai. Agar resolver ise referral maan le toh woh root par wapas jaayega, root phir test bhejega, test phir lame.test -- loop, budget tak.

classify() mein check: referral sirf tab valid hai jab cut humare zone ke strictly neeche ho aur name cut ke neeche: '!isSubdomain(cut, zone) || !isSubdomain(name, cut)' -> { kind: 'lame', why: 'referral to "." from zone "lame.test"' }. Upar (root) aur side (sibling zone, jaise lame.test se other.test) dono pakde jaate hain. Doosra lame shape: NOERROR, kuch nahi, AA=0 aur SOA bhi nahi -> 'empty non-authoritative response'. Yeh NODATA nahi maana jaata, kyunki ek non-authoritative server ka 'kuch nahi' negative cache karne layak proof nahi hai.

Handling: askZone lame ko failure maanta hai, trace mein 'lame (...), next server', aur agla server try karta hai. Test 'a lame server that refers us back UP (to the root) is skipped': lame.test ka ek hi server hai, hook usse root ka NS aur glue bhejwata hai, result SERVFAIL with reason matching /lame/. Mutation R6 (upward/sideways referral accept karna) isi test ne pakda. Note: lame server yaad nahi rakha jaata (README: remembering lame servers NOT implemented).
why_needed: Misconfigured zones internet par aam hain (domain transfer ke baad purane NS). Inhe pehchaan na paana = loops ya galat answers.
real_world_analogy: Aap ek office ke room 301 mein gaye, wahan baitha aadmi bolta hai 'main gate par jaake poocho' -- jahan se aap aaye the. Smart insaan samajh jaata hai ki yeh aadmi kaam ka nahi, aur room 302 try karta hai.
how_it_works: Downward rule: zone Z ke server ka referral sirf Z ke neeche aur qname ke upar ho. Violation -> lame -> askZone next server. Empty + AA=0 + no SOA -> lame.
in_this_project: src/resolver.ts classify: lame returns; askZone: 'if (out.kind === "lame")'. Fixture: lame.test -> ns.lame.test (LAME_IP 192.0.2.30). Test hook: answers [], authority [NS('', 'a.root-servers.test')], additional [A('a.root-servers.test', ROOT_IP)], aa false.
advantages: Loops shuru hone se pehle hi ruk jaate hain
Glue ke through upward poisoning (root ka nakli address) ka raasta band
Lame aur NODATA ka saaf farak
disadvantages: Lame server ko har lookup mein dobara try kiya jaata hai
Ek zone ke saare servers lame ho toh parent se dobara poochne ki koshish nahi
common_mistakes: Har NS-wala authority section ko referral maan lena
Non-authoritative empty response ko NODATA cache karna
Budget ko hi loop protection maan lena (kaam karta hai lekin bahut queries baad)
follow_up_questions: Sideways referral (sibling zone) kab legit ho sakta hai?
Lame servers ko kitni der ke liye 'bad list' mein rakhoge?

question: Trace what happens when the resolver meets the glueless delegation loop loop1.test <-> loop2.test. Which limit stops it, and what reason does the client see?
answer_hinglish:
Setup (test/fixtures.ts): test TLD mein NS('loop1.test', 'ns.loop2.test') aur NS('loop2.test', 'ns.loop1.test'), koi glue nahi. Matlab loop1 ka server ka address jaanne ke liye loop2 resolve karna padega, aur loop2 ke liye loop1.

Code padh ke walk: www.loop1.test -> root (referral test, glue) -> test (referral loop1.test, hosts [ns.loop2.test], glue khaali kyunki test ne koi A nahi bheja). serversFor: glue nahi, cache nahi, depth 0 < maxDepth -> nested resolveChain('ns.loop2.test', A, depth 1). Ab closestServers 'test' ka cached cut deta hai (root skip), test bolta hai 'loop2.test ka NS ns.loop1.test' -> serversFor depth 1 -> nested ns.loop1.test depth 2 -> ... har level par ek query test server ko. Jab depth maxDepth (4) tak pahunchti hai, serversFor throw karta hai 'NS lookups nested deeper than 4'.

Ab unwinding interesting hai: har upper serversFor apne nested resolveChain ka ResolveError pakadta hai (.catch -> undefined, 'try the next NS host'), uske paas aur host nahi, toh woh apna error fenkta hai: 'no address found for any NS host: ...'. Isliye top-level reason aksar 'no address found' hota hai, 'deeper than' nahi. Test isliye regex /deeper than|budget|no address/ use karta hai aur queries <= 40 assert karta hai (maxQueries 40 diya gaya).

Lesson: yeh loop do limits mein se koi bhi rok sakta hai. Isi wajah se mutations R8 (budget hataya) aur R9 (depth hataya) akele pakde nahi gaye -- doosri limit bacha leti thi. Fix: do naye tests jo har limit ko akela pin karte hain.
why_needed: Delegation loops real misconfigurations mein hote hain aur attack bhi ho sakte hain; interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki tum recursion aur error unwinding ko trace kar sakte ho.
real_world_analogy: Do dost: A bolta hai 'mera address B ko pata hai', B bolta hai 'mera address A ko pata hai'. Aap A ke liye B dhoondhte ho, B ke liye A... Ek samajhdaar aadmi 4 chakkar ke baad ruk jaata hai aur bolta hai 'dono ka address nahi mila'.
how_it_works: resolveOne -> referral -> serversFor (depth d) -> resolveChain(host, A, depth d+1) -> resolveOne -> referral -> serversFor (d+1) ... -> depth == maxDepth -> throw -> catch in parent -> no more hosts -> throw 'no address found' -> ... -> resolve() SERVFAIL.
in_this_project: src/resolver.ts serversFor ka .catch((e) => { if (e instanceof ResolveError) return undefined; throw e; }) aur 'if (ctx.budget.queries >= this.maxQueries) break;'. Test 'a delegation loop without glue (loop1.test <-> loop2.test) ends in SERVFAIL, within the budget'. README mutation section R8/R9 explanation.
advantages: Loop bounded, hang nahi
Ek NS host fail ho toh agla try hota hai
Budget shared hone se nested levels mein bhi total cap
disadvantages: Asli wajah (depth) top-level reason mein chhup jaati hai
Har level par test server ko dobara wahi sawaal (no negative 'unresolvable NS' cache)
common_mistakes: Sochna ki depth limit ka error hi client tak pahunchega
Nested lookup ko apna naya budget dena
Ek test se do limits 'cover' maan lena
follow_up_questions: Root cause reason preserve karne ke liye error chaining kaise karoge?
Loop detection visited-set se karoge ya limits se? Kyun?
'Unresolvable NS host' ko thodi der cache karna chahiye?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Limits-based termination simple aur generic hai (har tarah ke loop par chalta hai); visited-set exact loop pakadta lekin lambi non-repeating chains nahi rokta. Code dono kaam limits se karta hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Reason message misleading ho sakta hai; operator ko trace chahiye ('no glue: resolving NS host ...' lines ki ginti) asli depth dekhne ke liye.
advanced.alternatives: Visited (zone, host) set per resolution; error cause chaining (new ResolveError(msg, { cause })); NS-host-unresolvable negative cache.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Bahut saare clients ek hi broken domain poochein toh har ek poora loop chalayega (no dedupe, no negative cache for the failure) -- upstream par multiplied load.
advanced.production_improvements: SERVFAIL ko thodi der cache karna (RFC 9520 jaisa idea), root-cause reason preserve karna, metrics per limit.

question: A lookup returns SERVFAIL. How do you use the trace option and the reason field to find out why?
answer_hinglish:
Pehla step: ek akela lookup trace ke saath chalao: 'node dist/index.js resolve <name> [type]'. CLI Resolver ko trace: console.log ke saath banata hai aur end mein summary deta hai: ';; SERVFAIL, N upstream queries, T ms (reason)'. Server mode mein TRACE=1 environment variable wahi lines har client query ke liye print karta hai.

Phir trace lines padho, har ek code mein ek jagah se aati hai:
- '  ns1.alpha.test (192.0.2.1) UDP www.alpha.test A: NOERROR' -- exchange, ek query aur uska rcode ('TC' bhi dikhega agar truncated).
- 'referral test -> alpha.test (ns1.alpha.test, ns2.alpha.test)' -- resolveOne, ek level neeche.
- 'no glue: resolving NS host ...' -- serversFor nested lookup.
- '  <server>: SERVFAIL, next server' / ': lame (...), next server' / timeout message -- askZone failures.
- '  dropped N out-of-bailiwick record(s) ...' -- classify filter.
- '  ignored a UDP reply (mismatch) ...' -- transport ne spoof/garbage ignore kiya.

Reason se category pata chalti hai: 'all servers for zone "X" failed (ip: TimeoutError; ...)' = network ya dead servers (firewall par UDP 53 check karo); '... lame' = zone misconfigured; 'query budget of 60 used up' ya 'deeper than 4' = complex/looping delegation; 'CNAME chain longer than 8' = alias loop; 'more than 16 referrals' = broken referral chain.

Real example README se: gmail.com MX trace mein Google ne 10 '*.l.google.com' address records bheje aur sab 'dropped ... out-of-bailiwick' hue. Yeh bug nahi -- MX host ka address baad mein properly resolve hota hai. Trace ke bina yeh 'cache kyun nahi hua' wala confusion hota.
why_needed: DNS failures bahut layers mein ho sakte hain (network, zone config, spoofing, limits); ek line-per-decision trace ke bina andaza lagana padta.
real_world_analogy: Courier tracking: 'Delhi hub par pahuncha, Mumbai hub ko bheja, delivery boy ko diya, ghar band tha'. Sirf 'delivery failed' se kuch pata nahi chalta, har step ki line chahiye.
how_it_works: ResolverOptions.trace?: (line) => void; default no-op. Har decision point par this.trace(...). resolve() catch mein 'SERVFAIL name TYPE: message' aur Resolution.reason = e.message.
in_this_project: src/index.ts: resolve command (trace console.log) aur TRACE=1 server mode. src/resolver.ts mein saari this.trace calls. Tests trace ko array mein collect karte hain: out-of-bailiwick NS test 'no glue: resolving NS host ns.hoster.example' dhoondhta hai, bailiwick test 'dropped 3 out-of-bailiwick'. README mein real www.wikipedia.org trace.
code_example:
# real commands (README "Run it")
npm run build
node dist/index.js resolve www.wikipedia.org A    # every step printed, then ";; NOERROR, 5 upstream queries, ..."
TRACE=1 npm start                                 # stub server, prints every upstream query

Reason field client response ke saath programmatically milta hai
Tests trace lines par assert kar sakte hain
disadvantages: Free-text lines, structured logging (JSON) nahi
Busy server par TRACE=1 bahut noisy hoga, sampling nahi
common_mistakes: SERVFAIL dekh ke seedha upstream ko blame karna, trace nahi padhna
Dropped out-of-bailiwick records ko bug samajhna
nslookup se test karte waqt -port use karna (is Windows build mein ignore hota hai, README finding)
follow_up_questions: Production mein trace ko structured logs/metrics mein kaise badloge?
Ek specific client ki query ko trace karna ho toh kya jodoge?
Reason mein root cause chhup jaaye (no address found) toh kya karoge?

question: How do the resolver mutation checks R1-R11 map onto the algorithm, and why were R8 and R9 the only ones no test caught?
answer_hinglish:
Har R check resolver ke ek rule ko ek exact text replacement se todta hai, poora suite chalata hai, aur 'caught' tab hai jab kam se kam ek test red ho. Mapping: R1 TC ignore (exchange, 3 tests), R2 bailiwick filter off (classify, 2), R3 CNAME limit 1000 (resolveChain, 1), R4 timeout = lookup fail (askZone, 3), R5 SERVFAIL/REFUSED accept (askZone, 1), R6 lame check off (classify, 1), R7 glue answer rank (classify, 1), R10 RD=1 (exchange, 1), R11 cached CNAME not followed (resolveOne, 1). Nau pakde gaye, R8 (no query budget) aur R9 (no nesting limit) dono 0.

Investigation: dekha ki kaunsa test in limits ko touch karta hai -- sirf 'a delegation loop without glue (loop1.test <-> loop2.test) ends in SERVFAIL, within the budget'. Us test ka loop do limits mein se KOI bhi rok deta hai: budget hatao toh maxDepth 4 recursion rok deta hai (aur queries 40 se kam rehti hain), depth hatao toh budget 40 par rok deta hai. Aur assertion jaan boojh kar loose hai: reason /deeper than|budget|no address/. Isliye ek limit hatana observable behaviour nahi badalta -- redundant safety, single test.

Pattern: pakde gaye nau checks aise rules todte hain jo normal fixture lookups (TC, timeout, CNAME, glue) mein hamesha chalte hain. R8/R9 sirf pathological input par fire hone wale guards hain, aur dono ek hi scenario se cover the.

Fix: 'the query budget alone: maxQueries 2 ...' aur 'the nesting limit alone: maxDepth 0 ...' -- re-run par dono exactly naye test se pakde gaye. Coverage line hit kar leta; mutation ne dikhaya ki koi assertion us line par depend nahi karta.
why_needed: Safety limits wahi code hai jo normal tests mein kabhi trigger nahi hota; bina targeted tests ke koi refactor unhe chupchap hata sakta hai.
real_world_analogy: Ghar mein do taale hain. Aap test karte ho 'chor andar nahi aaya' -- pass. Lekin ek taala hata do, phir bhi pass, kyunki doosra kaafi tha. Har taale ko alag se check karna padega.
how_it_works: Mutation testing: source mein ek exact text replace, poora suite chalao, kam se kam ek red = caught. Overlapping guards ke liye har guard ka ek test jo baaki guards ko irrelevant bana de (chhota budget normal lookup par, depth 0 single nested lookup par).
in_this_project: test/resolver.test.ts mein dono tests ke upar comment: 'The delegation-loop test above is stopped by EITHER limit, so removing one of them alone was not caught (mutations R8 and R9). These two tests pin each limit separately.' README mutation table: R8/R9 '0 (not caught) -> 1 with the new test'.
advantages: Har limit ab independently protected
Tests chhote aur fast, fixture reuse
Mutation table mein gap aur fix dono documented
disadvantages: maxReferrals limit ka abhi bhi koi dedicated test nahi (mutation table mein bhi nahi)
Mutation checks manual hain, CI mein automated nahi
common_mistakes: Coverage % ko test quality maan lena
Loose regex assertion se 'kuch bhi fail ho, pass' bana dena
Ek scenario test se kai guards cover maan lena
follow_up_questions: maxReferrals ke liye isi tarah ka test kaise likhoge?
Mutation testing ko CI mein kaise automate karoge (Stryker jaisa tool)?
W4 'equivalent mutant' kya hota hai aur use kaise pehchaanoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Mutation checks haath se (41 checks) sasti aur focused hain; Stryker jaisa automated tool zyada mutants banata lekin slow aur noisy. Yahan hand-picked mutants har documented rule ke liye the.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar yeh gap na pakda jaata, koi refactor (jaise budget ko per-nested-lookup bana dena) chupchap amplification attack surface khol deta, aur suite green rehta.
advanced.alternatives: Property-based tests (random delegation graphs, assert queries <= maxQueries), ya assertion on exact reason per limit.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Code badhne par manual mutation list scale nahi karti; automated mutation testing nightly CI mein, sirf changed files par.
advanced.production_improvements: maxReferrals aur maxCnameChain=links boundary ke liye bhi isolated tests, CI mein mutation run, aur har ResolveError message ka ek test.

question: Why does askZone shuffle a zone's servers randomly instead of trying them in order or picking the fastest one?
answer_hinglish:
Default shuffle: true -- har askZone call servers ki ek nayi random order banata hai (Fisher-Yates, crypto.randomInt se) aur unhe us order mein try karta hai. Teen options the:

1. Fixed order (jaise list mein aaye): simple, lekin har resolver hamesha pehle server ko maarta hai -- load unequal, aur agar pehla server dead hai toh HAR lookup pehle uska timeout khaayega. 13 root hints mein se hamesha a.root par jaana bhi galat citizenship hai.
2. Random: load roughly barabar baant jaata hai, aur dead server ka cost lookups ke ek hisse par padta hai, sab par nahi. Koi state nahi rakhni padti. Spoofing ke liye bhi thoda accha: attacker ko pata nahi kis server ki taraf query jaayegi (asli defence random port + ID hai, yeh bonus hai).
3. RTT-based (Unbound/BIND style, smoothed RTT per server): sabse fast, dead servers avoid, lekin per-server state, decay, aur exploration logic chahiye. README honest list mein: 'Server selection by RTT, remembering lame/dead servers' NOT implemented.

Main random chunta: correctness aur simplicity ke liye yeh sahi middle ground hai, aur RTT selection ek clean add-on hai (askZone ke order line par).

Testing angle: randomness tests ko flaky bana deti -- 'ALPHA1 drop, ALPHA2 answer' wala test tabhi deterministic hai jab order fixed ho. Isliye ResolverOptions mein shuffle option hai aur test helper resolver() shuffle: false pass karta hai. Production default true.
why_needed: Ek zone ke saare servers par load aur failure ka asar kaise baante, yeh resolver ki citizenship aur latency dono decide karta hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek building mein teen lifts hain. Har koi pehli lift ka button dabaye toh woh overload, aur kharab ho toh sab atke. Random lift choose karo toh load barabar. Smart building system (RTT) jaanta hai kaunsi lift abhi sabse paas hai.
how_it_works: askZone: const order = this.shuffle ? shuffled(servers) : servers. shuffled(): copy, phir i = n-1 se 1 tak, j = randomInt(0, i + 1), swap.
in_this_project: src/resolver.ts askZone aur shuffled(); ResolverOptions.shuffle ('randomise the order servers of a zone are tried in, default true'). test/resolver.test.ts helper: new Resolver({ rootHints: FAKE_ROOT_HINTS, route: fake.route, timeoutMs: 1000, shuffle: false, ...opts }).
advantages: Stateless aur simple
Load spread aur failure spread
Tests ke liye switch off ho sakta hai
disadvantages: Fast server ko prefer nahi karta
Dead server ka cost random lookups par baar baar
common_mistakes: Array.sort(() => Math.random() - 0.5) se shuffle (biased)
Original array ko mutate kar dena (code copy banata hai)
Tests mein randomness chhod dena aur flaky tests
follow_up_questions: RTT tracking kaise implement karoge aur exploration kaise rakhoge?
Fisher-Yates kyun, sort-with-random kyun nahi?
shuffle: false production mein kab theek hai?

question: How would you justify the default limits (60 queries, 8 CNAME links, NS lookups 4 deep, 16 referrals, 2000 ms timeout), and what does each trade off?
answer_hinglish:
Har limit ek sawaal ka jawab hai: 'legit traffic ko kitni jagah chahiye aur attacker ko kitni milni chahiye?'

- maxQueries 60: ek resolution ke saare upstream queries, nested samet. Normal cold lookup 3-6 queries ka hai (fixtures: 3 aur 6; README wikipedia trace: 5). 60 ek CNAME chain plus kuch out-of-bailiwick NS lookups plus kuch dead servers ke liye kaafi room hai, lekin ek malicious zone ek client query se sau-hazaar queries nahi karwa sakta.
- maxCnameChain 8: real CNAME chains typically 1-3 links (CDN aliases). 8 kaafi hai; loop ka koi visited-set nahi, isliye yahi limit loop ko rokti hai ('a CNAME loop is SERVFAIL, not a hang').
- maxDepth 4: nested NS-address lookups. Ek out-of-bailiwick NS ka NS bhi out-of-bailiwick ho -- 2 level real mein ho jaata hai, 4 se zyada lagbhag hamesha misconfiguration ya loop.
- maxReferrals 16: comment kehta hai: naam mein max 127 labels hote hain, real chains 3-5 deep. 16 deep hierarchies ke liye bhi room.
- timeoutMs 2000: lamba timeout = dead server par zyada wait; chhota = slow lekin zinda server ko dead maan lena (especially door wale roots). Fixed hai, adaptive nahi.

Trade-off ka asli shape: limits chhoti = safer aur fast failure, lekin kuch legit complex domains SERVFAIL; badi = compatible lekin abuse ka room. Kyunki yeh options hain (ResolverOptions), tests chhote values (maxQueries 2, maxDepth 0, maxCnameChain 10) se boundaries pin karte hain.

Honest point: yeh defaults kisi measurement se nahi aaye; yeh BIND/Unbound jaise resolvers ke typical order of magnitude ke hain, aur code comments mein unka reasoning likha hai.
why_needed: Senior interview mein 'magic numbers kahan se aaye?' zaroor poocha jaata hai; jawab mein legit traffic ka shape aur abuse ka cost dono hone chahiye.
real_world_analogy: Office expense policy: ek trip par 60 auto rides tak allowed, 8 baar 'doosre office jao' redirects, 4 level 'pehle uska address pata karo'. Kam rakhoge toh genuine complicated trips ruk jaayengi, zyada rakhoge toh koi misuse karega.
how_it_works: Constructor defaults: timeoutMs ?? 2000, maxQueries ?? 60, maxCnameChain ?? 8, maxDepth ?? 4, maxReferrals ?? 16. Check points: askZone, resolveChain, serversFor, resolveOne. Sab ResolveError -> SERVFAIL.
in_this_project: src/resolver.ts ResolverOptions doc comments aur constructor. src/index.ts TIMEOUT_MS env var (default 2000). Tests: CNAME 'exactly the limit works' (c3 = 8 links OK, c1 = 10 links SERVFAIL, maxCnameChain 10 par 12 answers), maxQueries 2, maxDepth 0, delegation loop with maxQueries 40.
advantages: Har limit configurable aur alag test
Defaults ka reasoning code mein likha
Legit traffic ke liye kaafi headroom
disadvantages: Defaults measured nahi, judgement hain
Fixed timeout, adaptive nahi
Per-referral fan-out ka alag cap nahi
common_mistakes: Limits ko magic numbers chhod dena bina reasoning ke
Ek limit badhane ka asar doosre par na sochna (zyada CNAME links = zyada queries = budget)
Timeout bahut chhota rakh ke slow servers ko dead maan lena
follow_up_questions: Inme se kaunsi limit production metrics dekh ke tune karoge aur kaunsa metric?
Overall wall-clock deadline per resolution kyun jodoge?
Agar ek bada customer ka domain 9 CNAME links ka ho toh?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Static limits simple aur predictable; adaptive limits (per-zone history) better UX lekin state aur complexity. Yahan sab static, options se overridable.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Limit chhoti ho toh legit domain SERVFAIL (customer complaint, 'DNS down'); badi ho toh ek attacker domain resolver ko upstream amplifier bana deta hai.
advanced.alternatives: Wall-clock deadline (jaise 10 s per resolution) count limits ke saath; per-zone adaptive timeouts; NS fan-out cap per referral.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada traffic par per-resolution limits ke saath global limits bhi chahiye: total upstream QPS, per-client QPS, per-zone concurrency. Warna 'har resolution limit ke andar' hote hue bhi total load bahut.
advanced.production_improvements: Metrics se tune karna: queries per resolution ka histogram, kitni resolutions kis limit se ruki, timeouts per server; adaptive timeout (RTT ka multiple).

question: A team reports that lookups for their domain are sometimes 2 seconds slow and occasionally fail. Their zone has two nameservers and one is down. Walk through what this resolver does and what you would change.
answer_hinglish:
Is code mein kya hota hai: domain ka zone cut (NS set + glue) cache mein hai, toh closestServers seedha un do servers ko deta hai. askZone har baar shuffled() se order banata hai -- toh lagbhag aadhe cold lookups pehle dead server ko jaate hain, poora timeoutMs (default 2000 ms) wait karte hain, trace mein timeout line aati hai, phir zinda server se answer. Baaki aadhe fast. Yahi '2 seconds sometimes' hai. Answer cache ho jaane ke baad TTL tak sab 0 queries -- isliye problem answer TTL expire hone par baar baar dikhti hai, lagatar nahi.

'Occasionally fail' kab: (1) zinda server bhi us waqt slow/packet loss -- dono fail, 'all servers for zone ... failed (ip: TimeoutError; ip: TimeoutError)'; (2) client ka apna timeout (OS stub typically 1-5 s) hamare 2 s + doosri query se pehle khatam; (3) agar NS out-of-bailiwick hain aur unka hoster bhi wahi dead server hai, nested lookup bhi timeout khaata hai.

Investigate: 'node dist/index.js resolve <name>' kai baar chalao, trace mein dekho kaunsa IP timeout deta hai aur summary mein ms; server mode mein TRACE=1.

Fix -- domain team ke liye: dead NS ko theek karo ya parent (registrar) se delegation se hatao; NS alag networks par rakho. Resolver ke liye (README NOT implemented): dead/lame servers ko kuch der yaad rakhna (askZone failure par 'bad until' timestamp, order mein peeche), RTT-based selection, adaptive timeout, prefetch/serve-stale taaki TTL expiry par client ko wait na karna pade. Short-term knob: TIMEOUT_MS chhota karna -- lekin door wale slow servers par false timeouts badhenge.
why_needed: Yeh sabse common real DNS complaint hai; interviewer dekhta hai ki tum symptom ko code path (shuffle + sequential timeout + TTL) se jod sakte ho.
real_world_analogy: Do cashier hain, ek so raha hai. Har customer random cashier chunta hai; aadhe customers pehle 2 minute soye cashier ke saamne khade rehte hain, phir doosre ke paas jaate hain. Manager ko chahiye ki soye cashier ke counter par 'band' board laga de (remember dead server).
how_it_works: closestServers -> cached cut -> askZone(shuffled) -> exchange -> TimeoutError after timeoutMs -> next server -> answer -> cache for TTL -> TTL expire -> repeat.

question: Read resolveChain: exactly how many CNAME links are allowed, and how does it handle a CNAME loop?
answer_hinglish:
resolveChain(qname, qtype, ctx) ek loop hai: resolveOne se outcome lo; cname hai toh chain mein push karo aur target par jao; answer hai toh { NOERROR, answers: [...chain, ...rrs] }; negative hai toh { rcode, answers: chain, authority: soa }. Koi aur outcome (referral/lame resolveOne se bahar nahi aana chahiye) -> ResolveError 'unexpected outcome'.

Limit check: 'if (links >= this.maxCnameChain) throw' -- yeh check CNAME push karne se PEHLE hota hai, aur links 0 se shuru. Toh maxCnameChain 8 par links 0..7 = exactly 8 CNAME links allowed; 9th CNAME (links = 8) par SERVFAIL 'CNAME chain longer than 8 at <name>'. Test 'a CNAME chain longer than maxCnameChain is SERVFAIL; exactly the limit works' boundary pin karta hai: c3.alpha.test (c3 -> ... -> c10 -> www = 8 links) NOERROR, c1.alpha.test (10 links) SERVFAIL, aur maxCnameChain 10 par c1 ke 12 answers (10 CNAME + 2 A).

Loop handling: koi visited-set nahi. loopa -> loopb -> loopa ... bas chain limit tak chalta hai aur wahi error deta hai ('a CNAME loop is SERVFAIL, not a hang', reason /CNAME chain/). Accha side effect: fake authoritative server same-zone CNAMEs ko ek response mein chase karta hai, classify poora answers section cache kar deta hai, aur agle links resolveOne ke cached-CNAME check se 0 queries mein aate hain.

Note: CNAME target ko resolveOne normal naam ki tarah resolve karta hai -- doosre zone mein ho toh closestServers wahan se shuru karta hai ('a CNAME into another zone is followed from the root of that zone'). Mutation R3 (limit 1000) test ne pakda.
why_needed: Off-by-one limits interview mein code-reading ka classic test hai; aur CNAME loop ka handling batata hai ki tumne termination socha ya nahi.
real_world_analogy: Aap kisi ko dhoondh rahe ho, har aadmi bolta hai 'woh ab doosre naam se jaana jaata hai'. 8 baar naam badalne ke baad aap ruk jaate ho -- chahe naam repeat ho rahe ho (loop) ya bas lambi kahani ho.
how_it_works: for (links = 0; ; links++): out = resolveOne(name) -> cname: check links >= max, push, name = target -> answer/negative return. ctx share hota hai, budget bhi chain ke saare links ka.
in_this_project: src/resolver.ts resolveChain. Fixtures: chain = c1..c10 -> www.alpha.test, loopa <-> loopb, to-beta.alpha.test -> www.beta.test, dangling.alpha.test -> nothing.alpha.test. Tests: 'a CNAME answered together with its target in one response', 'a CNAME into another zone is followed from the root of that zone', chain limit test, loop test.

Chain client ko poori milti hai (CNAMEs + final RRset)
Cross-zone CNAME bina special code ke
disadvantages: Loop ko jaldi detect nahi karta (8 links tak chalta hai)
Error mein loop vs lambi chain ka farak nahi
common_mistakes: '>' aur '>=' mein off-by-one
Visited-set se loop rokna lekin lambi chain bhool jaana
Negative case mein CNAME chain gira dena (client ko alias dikhna chahiye)
