question: How does resolve() turn internal errors into a SERVFAIL response, and why does it rethrow some errors?
answer_hinglish:
resolve() public entry point hai aur ek try/catch mein resolveChain chalata hai. Agar error ResolveError (hamari apni 'resolution nahi ho paayi' errors: budget, depth, referrals, CNAME chain, saare servers fail, no NS address) ya WireError (koi malformed response jo TCP par decode na hua) hai, toh woh client ke liye ek normal Resolution banata hai: rcode SERVFAIL, answers aur authority khaali, queries = ab tak ki ginti, aur reason = e.message. Saath mein ek trace line 'SERVFAIL <name> <TYPE>: <message>'.

Koi aur error (TypeError, socket ka koi ajeeb error, programming bug) rethrow hota hai. Kyun? Kyunki SERVFAIL ka matlab hai 'DNS ki duniya mein kuch toot gaya' -- upstream servers, zone config, limits. Ek code bug ko SERVFAIL ke peeche chhupa doge toh tests aur logs mein kabhi dikhega nahi; har lookup chupchap fail hoga. Rethrow karne se test turant red hota hai aur stub server (src/server.ts) apne level par decide karta hai ki kya karna hai.

Do aur details: queries hamesha return hota hai, success par bhi failure par bhi, kyunki ctx.budget ek object hai jo poori resolution mein update hota hai -- yahi field tests use karte hain ('queries).toBe(3)', budget test mein toBe(2)). Aur ResolveError ek simple subclass hai: 'class ResolveError extends Error { override name = "ResolveError" }' -- naam se instanceof check reliable aur readable.
why_needed: Error ko client-facing rcode mein map karna har protocol server ka basic kaam hai; galat mapping se ya toh bugs chhupte hain ya client ko crash milta hai.
real_world_analogy: Restaurant mein agar dish ka ingredient khatam hai toh waiter politely bolta hai 'aaj yeh available nahi' (SERVFAIL). Lekin agar kitchen mein aag lagi hai toh woh chupchap 'available nahi' nahi bolta -- manager ko bulata hai (rethrow).
how_it_works: try { resolveChain } catch (e) { if ResolveError | WireError -> trace + SERVFAIL Resolution with reason; else throw }. Ctx object closure mein, isliye catch mein bhi queries count available.
in_this_project: src/resolver.ts resolve() aur ResolveError class; Resolution interface (rcode, answers, authority, queries, reason?). Tests reason par regex lagate hain: /budget of 2/, /deeper than 0/, /lame/, /CNAME chain/, /all servers for zone "alpha.test" failed/.
advantages: Expected failures client ko proper DNS rcode
Bugs chhupte nahi
reason field se tests aur operators dono ko wajah pata
disadvantages: reason sirf aakhri error ka message, root cause chain nahi
Rethrown errors ke liye caller (server) ko handling likhni padti hai
common_mistakes: catch (e) { return SERVFAIL } -- sab nigal jaana
queries count sirf success par return karna
Error class ka name set na karna (logs mein sirf 'Error')
follow_up_questions: Stub server rethrown error par client ko kya bhejna chahiye?
Error cause chaining yahan kaise jodoge?

question: How are CNAMEs combined with negative answers handled: a CNAME to a missing name, a CNAME into another zone, and what is not handled?
answer_hinglish:
Teen cases:

1. CNAME jiska target exist nahi karta (dangling.alpha.test -> nothing.alpha.test). Expected result: rcode NXDOMAIN, lekin answer mein CNAME (RFC 6604: rcode chain ke aakhri naam ka hota hai). Is code mein: resolveChain CNAME push karta hai, target ke liye resolveOne NXDOMAIN negative deta hai, aur return { rcode: NXDOMAIN, answers: chain }. Test 'a CNAME whose target does not exist: NXDOMAIN, with the CNAME in the answer'.

2. Server CNAME aur NXDOMAIN ek hi response mein bheje (real authoritative servers same-zone target ke liye aisa karte hain). classify ka NXDOMAIN branch pehle dekhta hai ki answers mein hamare naam ka CNAME hai ya nahi; hai toh cname outcome lautata hai aur poora answer cache karta hai -- naam ko NXDOMAIN cache NAHI karta, kyunki alias toh exist karta hai. Target phir apni lookup se negative milta hai. Fixture ka fake server CNAME case mein rcode NOERROR bhejta hai, isliye is branch ka alag test hai: "a server that sends rcode NXDOMAIN together with the CNAME: the chain is still followed" -- hook rcode ko NXDOMAIN bana deta hai aur resolver phir bhi nothing.alpha.test poochta hai.

3. CNAME doosre zone mein (to-beta.alpha.test -> www.beta.test). Fake alpha server target chase nahi karta (zone ke bahar), resolveOne target ke liye closestServers se naya walk shuru karta hai -- beta.test ke liye out-of-bailiwick nested lookup bhi. Test 'a CNAME into another zone is followed from the root of that zone'. Bailiwick yahan bhi kaam karta hai: agar alpha server www.beta.test ka A bhi bhej de toh woh drop hota hai.

NOT handled (README): 'CNAME + NXDOMAIN from a non-final zone' ka special handling, DNAME (raw rdata, ignored), aur wildcard synthesis.
why_needed: CNAMEs CDN aur SaaS mein har jagah hain; negative + CNAME combo galat handle hua toh client ko ya toh galat NXDOMAIN milta hai ya alias chhup jaata hai.
real_world_analogy: Aap ek purane address par gaye, wahan board hai 'shift ho gaye, naya address yeh'. Naye address par gaye -- wahan koi ghar hi nahi. Report mein dono likhoge: 'board mila tha (CNAME), aur naya address exist nahi karta (NXDOMAIN)'.
how_it_works: NXDOMAIN response: CNAME for name ? cache answers + cname outcome : putNegative(NXDOMAIN). resolveChain: negative outcome -> { rcode, answers: chain }. Cross-zone: next link resolveOne -> closestServers(target).
in_this_project: src/resolver.ts classify NXDOMAIN branch comment: 'The CNAME part of an NXDOMAIN response (alias exists, its target does not) is followed by the caller; here we only learn that name does not exist if no CNAME for it came along.' resolveChain negative return. Fixtures: CNAME('dangling.alpha.test', 'nothing.alpha.test'), CNAME('to-beta.alpha.test', 'www.beta.test').
advantages: Alias ko kabhi NXDOMAIN cache nahi kiya jaata
Client ko chain + sahi rcode
Cross-zone CNAME general mechanism se
disadvantages: Server ke bheje NXDOMAIN ko target ke liye directly use nahi kiya jaata, ek extra query
NXDOMAIN+CNAME branch ka fixture test nahi
DNAME aur wildcards ka handling nahi
common_mistakes: CNAME wale NXDOMAIN response ko alias ka NXDOMAIN maan lena
Negative answer mein chain gira dena
Cross-zone CNAME target ko usi server se poochna (bailiwick violation)
follow_up_questions: Server ka bheja CNAME + target NXDOMAIN ek hi response mein ho toh extra query kaise bachaoge, safely?
Fake server ko RFC 6604 jaisa banane ke liye kya badloge aur kaunsa test likhoge?
DNAME support kahan jodoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Har CNAME target ko alag lookup se verify karna safe hai (bailiwick + sahi authority) lekin ek extra query; server ke same-zone NXDOMAIN ko trust karna fast lekin zone check zaroori.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar NXDOMAIN branch CNAME check na karta, alias naam per-name NXDOMAIN cache ho jaata aur uske saare types (A, AAAA, MX) SOA minimum tak toot jaate.
advanced.alternatives: Unbound jaisa: response ke CNAME chain ko scrub karke in-zone parts ko trust karna, last name ka rcode directly use karna.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: CDN-heavy traffic mein CNAME chains bahut common; har link ka cache hit ratio aur cross-zone walks query count decide karte hain, aur negative caching ka sahi key (target naam) zaroori.
advanced.production_improvements: NXDOMAIN+CNAME fixture aur test, same-zone target ke negative ko directly use karna, DNAME (RFC 6672) support, wildcard awareness.

question: QNAME minimisation is not implemented. What privacy problem does it solve, and how would you add it to this resolution algorithm?
answer_hinglish:
Pehle honest baat: is project mein QNAME minimisation (RFC 9156) implement nahi hai; README NOT implemented list mein likha hai 'every server along the path sees the full name'. Aaj resolveOne har zone ko poora naam bhejta hai: root ko bhi 'www.secret-project.alpha.test A' dikhta hai, jabki root ko sirf itna jaanna chahiye ki 'test' kiska hai.

Problem: privacy. Root aur TLD operators ko poori query stream dikhti hai -- kaunse subdomains, kaunse services. Zaroorat sirf next label ki hai.

Kaise jodoge (askZone ka question badalna, resolveOne ka loop wahi):
1. resolveOne mein zone ke saath ek 'asked name' rakho: zone ke neeche ek label (zone '' -> 'test', 'test' -> 'alpha.test'). Jab tak asked name poora naam nahi, type NS (ya RFC 9156 ke mutabik A, kuch broken servers ki wajah se) poochho.
2. classify ka existing logic kaafi had tak chalega: referral aaya -> neeche jao; NODATA aaya (empty non-terminal ya zone cut nahi) -> same zone, ek label aur jodo; jab asked == name, asli type poochho.
3. NXDOMAIN intermediate name par: RFC 8020 kehta hai neeche bhi kuch nahi, toh poora naam NXDOMAIN. Lekin kuch broken servers empty non-terminals par galat NXDOMAIN dete hain -- isliye production resolvers 'relaxed' mode mein full name se dobara try karte hain.
4. Budget: zyada labels = zyada queries; maxQueries aur maxReferrals ko label count ke hisaab se sochna padega, aur ek 'max minimisation steps' limit chahiye (RFC suggestion: kuch labels ke baad seedha full name).

Fixtures pehle se kaam ke hain: sub.alpha.test empty non-terminal hai, jo exactly woh case test karega.
why_needed: Privacy aaj resolver design ka part hai; interviewer dekhta hai ki tum ek existing algorithm mein feature kahan aur kitne risk ke saath fit karoge.
real_world_analogy: Aap kisi building mein 'Room 507 ke Sharma ji' ko dhoondh rahe ho. Gate par poora naam batane ki zaroorat nahi -- sirf 'paanchvi manzil kahan hai?'. Manzil par pahunch ke 'room 507?', aur room par hi 'Sharma ji?'. Har level ko utna hi bataya jitna zaroori.
how_it_works: Current: askZone(zone, servers, fullName, type). Minimised: askZone(zone, servers, nextLabelName(zone, fullName), NS) until asked == fullName, then askZone(..., fullName, type). NODATA at intermediate = continue in same zone; referral = descend; NXDOMAIN = stop (with fallback).
in_this_project: src/resolver.ts resolveOne ka referral loop aur askZone(zone, servers, name, type, ctx) signature yahan modify honge. wire.ts ka parentName/isSubdomain next-label calculation mein kaam aayenge. Fixture host.sub.alpha.test empty non-terminal test 'NODATA: ... (and an empty non-terminal is NODATA too)' mein pehle se use hota hai.
advantages: Root/TLD operators ko kam data
Existing referral loop ka structure reuse
Empty non-terminal fixtures pehle se maujood
disadvantages: Zyada queries (har label ek), cold latency badhti hai
Broken servers ke liye fallback logic
NODATA vs referral classification aur nazuk ho jaati hai
common_mistakes: Naam ko '.' par split karna (escaped dots wale labels toot jaayenge)
Intermediate NXDOMAIN par fallback na rakhna
Budget limits ko adjust na karna
follow_up_questions: Intermediate queries ke liye NS type ya A type -- kyun?
QNAME minimisation aur aggressive NSEC caching ka kya rishta hai?
Kya iske saath cache ke zone cut logic mein kuch badlega?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Privacy vs performance aur compatibility: har label ek query, aur kuch purane servers ENT par galat jawab dete hain. Production 'relaxed' mode leta hai: fail ho toh full name.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Galat NXDOMAIN intermediate par -> poora subtree unresolvable (agar RFC 8020 aggressively follow kiya). NODATA ko galti se final maan liya -> galat negative cache.
advanced.alternatives: Full-name queries (aaj ka behaviour) + DNS-over-TLS/HTTPS to upstream (sirf on-path privacy); ya forwarding to a trusted resolver.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada traffic par zone cut cache hits ki wajah se minimisation ka extra cost sirf cold paths par; lekin root/TLD par query count badhega -- budget aur dedupe dono zaroori.
advanced.production_improvements: Relaxed mode with fallback, max-minimisation-labels limit, metrics for fallbacks, aur sub.alpha.test jaise ENT fixtures par tests.

question: maxReferrals has no dedicated test (it is not in the mutation table either). Write a test that pins it, and explain why your numbers are exact.
answer_hinglish:
Pehle code dekho: resolveOne ka loop 'for (let referrals = 0; referrals <= this.maxReferrals; referrals++)' hai. Har iteration ek askZone call. Referral mila toh zone neeche jaata hai aur referrals++; loop condition fail ho toh 'more than N referrals for <name>'.

www.alpha.test ka walk fixture mein: root -> referral (1) -> test -> referral (2) -> alpha.test -> answer. Matlab 2 referrals aur 3 askZone calls.

maxReferrals 1 ke saath: iteration 0 root referral deta hai, iteration 1 test referral deta hai (yeh dono loop ke andar process hote hain, serversFor bhi chalta hai), ab referrals = 2 > 1, loop khatam -> ResolveError 'more than 1 referrals for www.alpha.test'. Queries = 2 (alpha.test tak pahunchte hi nahi). maxReferrals 2 ke saath iteration 2 alpha.test ko poochta hai -> answer, NOERROR, 3 queries. Yeh exact boundary hai: 'N referrals allowed, N+1th referral ke baad fail'.

Do assertions dono taraf ka off-by-one pakadte hain: agar koi '<=' ko '<' kar de toh maxReferrals 2 wala case fail hoga; agar check hata de toh 1 wala NOERROR ban jaayega. Saath mein alpha.test server ke log ko check karna dikhata hai ki limit ke baad koi query nahi gayi. Test shuffle: false wale existing resolver() helper se chalega, fake network aur fixtures wahi. Reason regex budget/depth wale tests jaisa specific hona chahiye ('more than 1 referrals'), taaki doosri limit se fail hona test ko pass na kar de -- R8/R9 ka lesson.
why_needed: Ek safety limit bina test ke refactor mein chupchap gayab ho sakti hai; R8/R9 ne yahi dikhaya tha.
real_world_analogy: Lift mein 'max 2 floors per ride' rule test karna: ek aadmi 2 floor upar jaaye (allowed), doosra 3 floor (rokna chahiye). Dono test chahiye, warna rule '1 floor' ya 'unlimited' hone par pata nahi chalega.
how_it_works: Boundary testing: limit = (required - 1) -> fail with specific reason, limit = required -> success. Fixture ka known referral count (2) use karo.
in_this_project: test/resolver.test.ts ke 'walking down from the root' describe block mein, budget/depth tests ke bagal mein. Helpers: resolver(), addrs(), asked(), constants ALPHA1_IP. Code: src/resolver.ts resolveOne.
advantages: Dono taraf ka off-by-one pakda jaata hai
Specific reason regex, doosri limit se false pass nahi
Existing fixtures, koi naya setup nahi
disadvantages: Fixture ke referral count par depend karta hai; fixture badle toh numbers badlenge
common_mistakes: Sirf failure case test karna, success boundary nahi
Loose regex (/SERVFAIL|referral/) jo kisi bhi error par pass ho
fake.reset() bhool jaana, toh asked() pichhle run ke logs dikhaayega

question: Implement a small 'remember dead servers' feature in askZone: a server that timed out is tried last for the next 60 seconds. Show the code and a test.
answer_hinglish:
Problem (README NOT implemented): 'a dead server costs a full timeout on every lookup that picks it first'. Chhota fix: Resolver ek Map<ip, untilMs> rakhe. askZone mein TimeoutError aaye toh us IP ko 60 s ke liye 'bad' mark karo. Order banate waqt pehle shuffle (ya fixed order), phir stable sort jisme bad servers peeche. Important design rules:

1. Bad server ko hataana nahi, sirf peeche rakhna. Agar saare servers bad hain (network blip), tab bhi sabko try karna hai -- warna ek blip poore zone ko 60 s ke liye maar dega.
2. Success par mark hatao (server wapas aa gaya).
3. Clock inject karo (cache ki tarah 'now' option), taaki test sleep na kare.
4. Sirf TimeoutError aur TransportError par mark karo; SERVFAIL/REFUSED/lame zone-specific ho sakte hain -- ek server ek zone ke liye lame aur doosre ke liye sahi ho sakta hai, isliye unhe ip-level ban nahi.

Test fixture ke ALPHA1 drop hook se: pehla resolve ALPHA1 ka timeout khaata hai (shuffle: false, toh ALPHA1 pehle), doosre resolve (different name, taaki cache answer na de) mein ALPHA1 ko query hi nahi jaani chahiye, aur time timeoutMs se kaafi kam. Phir clock 60 s aage -- ALPHA1 phir pehle try hota hai.

Yeh ek simplified version hai; production resolvers (Unbound infra cache) RTT bhi rakhte hain, exponential backoff, aur probing karte hain. Main yahi chhota version recommend karunga kyunki yeh askZone ke order line aur catch block mein fit hota hai, baaki algorithm untouched.
why_needed: Dead NS sabse common production latency complaint hai; yeh exercise dikhata hai ki state ko bina correctness tode kaise jodte ho.
real_world_analogy: Office mein jo colleague do baar phone nahi uthata, aap use list mein last kar dete ho -- delete nahi karte, kyunki shayad woh wapas aa jaaye, aur baaki sab bhi na uthayein toh use bhi try karoge.
how_it_works: askZone: order = stableSortBy(isBad)(shuffled(servers)). catch TimeoutError/TransportError -> bad.set(ip, now + 60000). success -> bad.delete(ip). now() injectable.
in_this_project: Badlav src/resolver.ts askZone aur ResolverOptions mein; test test/resolver.test.ts mein existing 'a server that never answers times out and the next server of the zone is tried' ke pattern par (fake.get(ALPHA1_IP).hook = () => 'drop'). Yeh feature abhi repo mein NAHI hai.
advantages: Dead server ki latency sirf pehli baar
Demote not drop: blip par zone nahi marta
Injectable clock se fast deterministic test
disadvantages: Per-process state, restart par khatam
Fixed 60 s, adaptive backoff nahi
RTT nahi dekhta, sirf dead/alive
common_mistakes: Bad server ko list se hata dena (saare bad = zone unresolvable)
SERVFAIL/lame par bhi IP ban (zone-specific failure ko global bana dena)
Date.now() hard-code karke test mein sleep
follow_up_questions: Isko RTT-based selection mein kaise badhaoge?
Map ka size bound kaise karoge (bahut saare IPs)?
Cluster mein yeh state share karni chahiye?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Simple dead/alive memory vs full RTT infra cache: pehla 20 lines, doosra zyada fayda lekin decay, probing, aur tuning chahiye.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Bug se sab servers bad -> demote-not-drop rule ki wajah se phir bhi resolve hota hai. Network partition par saare IPs bad mark honge, recovery par 60 s tak order ulta-pulta (harmless).
advanced.alternatives: Smoothed RTT + timeout backoff (Unbound), hedged parallel query after short delay, ya health probing background mein.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Bahut saare zones/IPs par Map badhegi -- TTL-based cleanup ya size cap chahiye; multi-process par har process apna seekhega (thoda duplicate cost, lekin simple).
advanced.production_improvements: Exponential backoff, RTT tracking, metrics (bad servers count, timeouts avoided), aur cache ki tarah size limit.
